reader.identity: rr-euf2 isolated reader (Type 2 TASK, cold-read test)
reader.separation: Fresh subagent with no part in producing the files; opened only files inside the rr-euf2/in folder; no repository, git history, session, conversation or network used.

Q-1.statement: The owner decides, by act kind A16 ('decide': choose exactly one of four alternatives), whether the identified v4 candidate replaces the v3.0.1 fallback. The package is pkg:app-v4:replacement:FX-RP1-2 and calls itself a fixture not for presentation to the owner.

fields.subject_revision: ILLUSTRATIVE (SQ example; not a real candidate)

Q-2.statement: The package names no real revision: the subject revision and build are the placeholder 'ILLUSTRATIVE (SQ example; not a real candidate)', copied from the SQ dossier. The journey's candidate identification record does not supply an App candidate (no candidate identified; host joins deferred), so one candidate across both obligations is not established.

Q-3.statement: All seven elements are not_evidenced because none of the 15 counted step results resolves to a record of an identified candidate; six elements are recorded as passes and restart is recorded not-pass (S11-6 blocked). The obligation is not_evidenced and not established; V4-EXM-12 (model access, 6 steps) is set outside the core loop.

Q-4.statement: The journey obligation is incomplete: P20-A is not counted as a completed V4-EXM-20 witness (in this example LHQ-20 was not run), no acceptance act is cited and no independent review record exists for the journey. A host receipt (RC-1, invented) appears in the dossier's DEL-09-11 hand-over but not in its hand-over to DEL-11-03.

Q-5.statement: The replacement evidence is not complete: the core loop is not established, the journey is not established and the candidate is not reconciled across the two obligations.

Q-6.statement: The packet names six gaps: four stand before complete replacement evidence (restart, core-loop evidence, journey witness, joined candidate; suppliers DEL-09-02 and DEL-09-07, with the SWBPIPE owner) and two are carried for the owner but are not replacement conditions (continuity, DEL-11-01; adoption, DEL-11-02). Practitioner validation is not listed as a gap.

Q-7.statement: Only ALT-PUBLISHED ends v3.0.1's role as the published fallback, and it is also a public-release act the owner decides separately; ALT-OWN-USE replaces v3.0.1 only in the owner's own work while v3.0.1 stays the published fallback. No alternative retires anything.

Q-8.statement: The disposition record states the package was not presented (a fixture prepared only for the consumption check), no owner act exists or is implied, and v3.0.1 remains the fallback with old projects and archives kept.

Q-9.statement: No validation period or activities are agreed and no practitioner use has occurred; practitioner validation is stated not to be a replacement condition (R23-32 F-R3).

Q-10.statement: The packet says it never establishes a replacement decision, public release, retirement, professional reliance, consumer adoption or practitioner validation, whatever its evidence.

Q-11.statement: The thesis tree observed at the named commit matches the expected tree (committed-tree identity only); the v3.0.1 fallback identity was not re-checked against the remote release; continuing-obligation dispositions and consumer adoption status are not supplied, and the archive check was not run.

Q-12.statement: The whole packet is illustrative: it is built from schema examples and fixtures, and by its own definition nothing in it can establish an obligation.

issues.statement: The dispatch named READER_BRIEF.md and the reader-account schema's description cites READER_BRIEF.md, but the supplied file is READER_BRIEF.v2.md. Its hash matched the input-set list, so it was used as the brief.

issues.about: Alternatives that replace v3.0.1 are offered although the replacement conditions are not shown met
issues.statement: ALT-OWN-USE and ALT-PUBLISHED are offered as valid choices, but the packet says the replacement evidence is incomplete. AX-001 says no replacement qualification can be claimed until both witnesses hold, and open matter P-1 calls replacement 'an act, not a question now' until both witnesses exist. The files do not say whether choosing a replacing alternative before V4-REP-01's conditions hold is permitted. A decision maker could read the package as inviting an act that its own basis treats as premature.

ALT-OWN-USE replaces v3.0.1 in the owner's own work while saying v3.0.1 'remains the published fallback' for everyone else. Whether v3.0.1 still counts as 'the fallback' after this choice depends on the scope of that word, which the package does not define.

issues.about: Restart: recorded not-pass shown as not_evidenced
issues.statement: Restart is recorded as not passing (S11-6 blocked: 'route cannot delegate; no recording'), but its status is not_evidenced, the same as the six elements recorded as passes. The difference appears only in the 'recorded' field and gap G-CL-RESTART. A reader who looks only at status values would miss that one element has an adverse recorded result.

issues.about: Illustrative 'independent' review and 'pass' outcomes in the SQ dossier
issues.statement: The SQ dossier reports V4-EXM-10 'pass', reports the hand-over as independently examined, and the packet lists the dossier review as 'present' (EXP-RX-02). All of these are illustrative placeholders. A decider skimming these fields could take the core loop as independently reviewed and passed, although the packet treats it as not evidenced.

issues.about: Continuity input produced by the packet builder
issues.statement: S-4 (continuity) and S-5 (practitioner standing) were produced by DEL-11-03's own prototype builder, standing in for DEL-11-01 and DEL-09-12, with the standing first_cut_interface. The thesis 'matches' result is described as observed by read-only git, yet its attribution and nonbinding standing are not yet inspected, and its working bytes were not compared. The packet's assembler therefore supplies some of its own inputs.

issues.about: Fallback identity and the ALT-PUBLISHED consequence rest on unchecked or inferred facts
issues.statement: The fallback's identity (release, installer hash) was not re-checked against the remote release. ALT-PUBLISHED's consequence that v3.0.x installs would be offered v4 is labelled an inference from App v3's records, and that excerpt states it 'does not assert the latest remote release'. The core-loop v3 references come from a v3.0.0-era candidate that is not an ancestor of the v3.0.1 source.

Several identifiers are used without a definition in the packet's terms list, for example DEL-09-11 (receipt location 'handoff_del_09_11'), DEL-09-06, DEP-09-07-011, DEP-09-07-024, LHQ §7, U-SQ-5, WR TT-7, RP-R1 and RP-R7, EUF1-D1 and D2, D-11, U2, PEC and Domains. DH-1 and SQ-R8 are defined but not visibly applied in the supplied records, and VER-003 and VER-004 are defined but not excerpted.

issues.about: CIR lists host contributions as 'answered' while no candidate is identified
issues.statement: The CIR lists 13 SWBPIPE host contributions as 'answered' (citing relay answers that are not supplied), yet every candidate element is not_supplied and all activity bindings are unbound. A reader could overestimate how ready the host is. The cited evidence files are not in the input set.
Reuse rests on one counted step (J-7). Two further reuse passes (J-8R, J-9R) are recorded but not counted, for a reason that cites 'WR TT-7 (PROPOSED)', which is not explained in the supplied files.
